00 — THE RECORDIST

She listens
for a living.

Mara Voss has spent fifteen years carrying two microphones to the ends of the earth — glacier fronts, dying mill towns, forests that fall silent one spring at a time. She does not compose, direct, or restore. She arrives early, sits still, and keeps what the world says before it stops saying it. Forty-three countries. One rule: record it like it is the last time anyone will hear it. It usually is.

B. 1984 · SASKATCHEWAN · WORKS ALONE · NAGRA IV-S

04 — FIELD LOG

Dispatches made between recordings—weather, equipment, and the exact moment a sound changes status.

2026.03.11 — VATNAJÖKULL, ICELAND

Recorded the shelf at 3 a.m. Meltwater running under the crust, louder than last year. The ice is talking faster now.

DEGRADING

2025.11.02 — LARAMIE, WYOMING

The last coin-operated payphone on the line. Held the dial tone for six minutes before the exchange dropped it forever.

ARCHIVED

2025.06.19 — LANCASHIRE, ENGLAND

Loom shed no. 4 ran one final hour for the tape. The weavers stood in the doorway and listened with me.

ARCHIVED

2024.12.30 — TASMANIA

Returned to the grove. The pair that sang here is gone. Recorded thirty minutes of what remains: rain.

EXTINCT
05 — METHOD

Arrive early.Wait.Press record.

There is no directing in field recording — only attendance. I get there before the sound does, sit still long enough to be forgotten, and let the place speak at its own pace. The same two microphones for fifteen years. Patience is the third.
